The old card asked how thick Saturn's rings are, and review C is right that it could not work: the answer is a length in metres, every distractor is the same kind of number, and there is no picture of a ring's thickness that a child can judge — the only honest drawing is a razor-thin line, which is the answer printed on the card. The picture is the hardest brief in the file: a thick atmosphere is invisible, so the generator is told to draw no sky, no glow, no haze and no parent planet, because a glowing moon in a lit sky would be the answer. The choices are four real Saturn moons a child hears rather than reads; the three distractors are chosen over Rhea and Iapetus because a name with two accepted pronunciations cannot be read aloud fairly.
